articles.title: “My character has been attacked…”: Caleb Williams’ desire for motivation draws Michael Jordan comparisons amid Chicago Bears QB’s gridiron resurgence
articles.summary: Caleb Williams began his 2026 NFL season with one thought: to go beyond the playoffs. But two games in, he injured his hamstring.
articles.body: Caleb Williams began his 2026 NFL season with one thought: to go beyond the playoffs. But two games in, he injured his hamstring. Case Keenum and Tyson Bagent stepped up for him to hold the fort until he returned stronger than ever.He missed three games and returned for Weeks 6 and 7. A side of him that hadn’t been seen before was out in the open for everyone to see. He took all the criticism and adversity and turned it into a ball of motivation to grab back-to-back gridiron victories.Now, this competitive spirit has been witnessed by the sports world before - in NBA legend Michael Jordan.That’s what NBC Sports’ ProFootballTalk hosts Mike Florio and Chris Simms discussed: Caleb Williams’ ability to find motivation in criticism and adversity draws steadfast comparisons to basketball legend Michael Jordan’s fierce competitive mindset.Caleb Williams turns criticism into motivationFOX Sports host Colin Cowherd also defended Caleb Williams. Cowherd called Caleb a generational talent, a modern athlete. Cowherd argued that modern athletes are more emotional and heavily influenced by their online presence.The Chicago Bears quarterback faced unnecessary criticism after his hamstring injury. Cowherd previously defended Williams when he covered him during his USC days - for his fingernails and jumping into the stands to cry with his family after USC’s 10-point loss to Washington.The FOX Sports host then played a clip of Williams where the quarterback opened up about outside criticism that affected him during his hamstring injury recovery.The 24-year-old quarterback acknowledged that questions surrounding his toughness and character only motivated him further. However, his primary motivation had always been to return to the gridiron, help his teammates, and address the team’s recent struggles.“I care about the team, the organization, winning, being out there,my teammates, all of that. I care, and that’s the biggest thing,” Williams said. “This is what I love to do. This puts a smile on my face. It’s everything to me.So, not being able to be out there was frustrating. That was more of the tears, or whatever that was. The other half of it was everybody making jokes and all of that, but that doesn’t bother me.My character has been attacked…since for a while. And so, it’s just another motivating factor when I get out there and get going again.”The 2024 first-round first-overall pick’s comments depict his competitive spirit. He doesn’t allow criticism to distract him from his main goal.Much like his head coach, Ben Johnson, who didn’t even smile when his team’s player kicked a record-breaking field goal. Why? Because that game victory is temporary. He wants the Super Bowl. He wants the ultimate goal of playing football - the Lombardi Trophy.Why is Michael Jordan a fitting Caleb Williams comparison“He [Caleb Williams] does have an edge about him. And perspective. And an inner thought that’s very mature. And definitely, extremely motivated. Psycho in a good way type of guy. And he’s not content just being like the man.He wants to be The Greatest of All Times. He wants to be the [Michael] Jordan of Chicago and football. He embraces that,” Chris Simms told Mike Florio on NBC Sports’ Pro Football Talk’s Oct. 22 episode. Williams’ drive to improve through adversity mirrors Jordan’s competitive approach.Now, why is Michael Jordan a fitting comparison to Caleb Williams? The NBA legend built his legacy on relentless competitiveness, mental toughness, and a rare ability to transform slights into motivation.His competitive drive led the Chicago Bulls to win six NBA Championships during the 1990s. He became one of the most celebrated athletes in Chicago’s sports history. Williams, on the other hand, could be trying to become like him. He wants to create his own legacy with the Chicago Bears.Since he returned, he has posted his first two wins. He leads the league with a 72.5% completion rate after leading the Bears to a 30-24 win over the Drake Maye-led New England Patriots in Week 7.Maye is from the same 2024 draft class as that of Williams. Even though Maye has been to a Super Bowl and Williams hasn’t, that fact also could have become a motivating factor for the Chicago Bears quarterback in the Week 7 matchup. And we know that he won that too.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Super Bowl favorite Los Angeles Rams could eye WR market amid 2-4 record, Davante Adams’ IR stint, and Puka Nacua injury
articles.summary: All through the 2026 offseason, if you asked anyone, they would tell you the Super Bowl favorites were the Los Angeles Rams. The reason?
articles.body: All through the 2026 offseason, if you asked anyone, they would tell you the Super Bowl favorites were the Los Angeles Rams. The reason? Their blockbuster trade for Myles Garrett from the Cleveland Browns. Fast forward to today, and Garrett is currently on injured reserve.To top it off, Aaron Donald - the Super Bowl-winning defensive tackle - even came out of retirement just because the Rams traded for Garrett. Yet, Donald ended up missing Week 4 due to minor back soreness.Consequently, this deadly duo hasn’t played a single game together in the 2026 NFL season, failing to share the field when it mattered most to live up to those Super Bowl expectations. It’s a stark contrast: Donald won a ring for the Rams, while Garrett could never win one in Cleveland.Even NFL Insider Ari Meirov reported via X a few days ago, “Aaron Donald came out of retirement to play alongside Myles Garrett, Kobie Turner, and Poona Ford, among others. He’s currently on a 2-4 Rams team without any of them.”Rams explore WR trade market amid mounting injuriesMyles Garrett isn’t ready to come back and is still on IR. Kobie Turner is suffering from a groin injury and will be out for 4 to 6 weeks. Poona Ford suffered a ruptured triceps, and he’s out for the 2026 season.To add the cherry on top, star wide receiver Davante Adams suffered a ruptured hamstring in Week 6 loss to the Arizona Cardinals. He’s placed on IR and will be out for 6 to 10 weeks.So, here we are, exploring the trade market to strengthen the Rams’ receiving corps and revive their playoff hopes - if they have any left.When there’s no manpower, who will fight the battle when it matters most? Maybe Garrett is their hidden gem, but if the 2–4 record takes a turn for the worse, will they even make it to the big games?Anyhow, let’s check out the wide receiver market for the Rams, because depending on Puka Nacua is going to become heavier with every passing minute. He has only recorded 1 rushing touchdown and 1 receiving touchdown across 4 of his 6 games. Two games were missed due to a hip/groin injury.To top it off, Puka Nacua left Thursday's practice with a calf injury. Still, there’s a ray of hope even if there’s a cloud of doubt: NFL insider Ian Rapoport reported just hours ago that Nacua underwent testing on his calf, and it is believed to be minor.Puka Nacua injury update“I wouldn’t say precautionary, because it’s not nothing, but at least not a significant injury. What that doesn’t tell us is whether or not Puka Nacua will be able to play this weekend for the Los Angeles Rams. I think it’s safe to say Puka Nacua is up in the air for Sunday,” Ian Rapoport added.So, there goes another wide receiver. He could be listed as questionable for the Week 7 matchup vs. the Las Vegas Raiders.Now is the screaming time for the Rams to urgently target wide receivers - especially ahead of the November 10 NFL trade deadline. This one potential move could help the franchise turn its season around.Potential Rams WR targets before NFL trade deadlineAccording to Rams Wire’s Cameron DaSilva, the following eight wideouts could be considered before the trade deadline: Indianapolis Colts WR Josh Downs, Jacksonville Jaguars WR Brian Thomas Jr.,Minnesota Vikings WRs Jordan Addison and Jauan Jennings, Cleveland Browns WR Jerry Jeudy, Dallas Cowboys WR George Pickens, Washington Commanders WR Stefon Diggs, and Tampa Bay Buccaneers WR Chris Godwin.According to Pro Football Rumors’ Sam Robinson, Sean McVay’s suffering team could consider trading for Buffalo Bills WR Josh Palmer, Indianapolis Colts WR Keenan Allen, and Tennessee Titans WR Calvin Ridley.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Dan Campbell Responds to Sam LaPorta's Explosive Comments About Lions Contract Talks
articles.summary: Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell defended Sam LaPorta after the star tight end said he would consider playing elsewhere next season amid stalled extension negotiations.
articles.body:
Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell defended Sam LaPorta after the star tight end said he would consider playing elsewhere next season amid stalled extension negotiations.

Campbell told reporters LaPorta is "locked in" despite his comments ahead of the Lions' upcoming Week 7 matchup against the Green Bay Packers this Sunday.

"Look, I've said things that I regret... that doesn't mean that's who the person is," Campbell said Friday. "You say something, it's— sometimes you get something off your chest. But we pick the guys we pick for a reason, because we know their character, and we know that they're about deep down.

"Sam's a stud, alright? And he's going to help us win games. And he really is, he's an unselfish teammate, an unselfish player."

LaPorta said in a recent appearance on Pardon My Take he would "go get paid somewhere else" if he and the Lions weren't able to reach resolution on an extension.

"I break my f--king back for the team, and then I'm going out there this year, and I'm balling, and maybe they're just not showing the love," LaPorta said.

LaPorta underwent surgery on a herniated disc in his back last November. He has made 37 catches for 316 receiving yards and three touchdowns in his first five games back since the procedure.

Campbell said LaPorta's comments hadn't been a "distraction" in the Lions locker room since the podcast aired.

"You can never take anything personal when you start talking about business. That's why business and football, they don't belong with each other," Campbell said.

Campbell then showed frustration after more questions regarding LaPorta, at which point he told a reporter, "I said I didn't want it to be a distraction, and now it's becoming one, because you keep asking these things."

LaPorta is playing the season in the final year of his rookie deal. ESPN and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported earlier this month he and the Lions had paused contract talks.

The Lions do not have a policy again in-season contract talks, but Rapoport noted at the time "the thought is that a deal is unlikely considering the two sides couldn't reach an agreement over the first four weeks of the season."

The tight end market is currently led by the San Francisco 49ers' George Kittle, Arizona Cardinals' Trey McBride and Green Bay Packers' Tucker Kraft who each make in the neighborhood of $19 million per season. Rapoport previously reported he could see LaPorta potentially resetting the positional market when he signs his next deal.

articles.title: Donald Trump: US President says NFL Paris game on Sunday 'could have been postponed' amid civil unrest
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers are set to take on the New Orleans Saints in Paris - live on Sky Sports NFL from 1pm, Sunday (kick-off, 1.30pm); the French government are deploying a larger security presence in the city following a week of civil unrest, with further demonstrations planned
articles.body:
France is bracing for more demonstrations Saturday against the high cost of living, with museums closing and the government deploying a larger security presence to prevent a repeat of last week's violent unrest.

The game on Sunday - the first ever NFL regular-season game held in France - is taking place at Stade de France in Saint-Denis, just north of the capital.

"I think maybe it's looking like tomorrow is going to be a bad day in France, so you worry about it," Trump told reporters.

"I would have said the NFL could have probably postponed that match, because France is really in trouble."

The US State Department issued a security alert late on Thursday, saying: "Numerous groups submitted plans for protests on Saturday October 24. Americans in Paris for the NFL game on Sunday October 25, should also exercise caution and be aware of their surroundings.

"While permits may be filed for demonstration routes, last-minute changes can happen and protests can occur outside planned routes."

NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell said this week that preparations were made in consultation with US and French authorities.

Street protests, he said, "are not unusual in France". The league did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Trump's remarks.

Soccer team Paris Saint-Germain's game against Lyon has been moved from Sunday to Monday evening at the request of Paris police.

The game was scheduled for Sunday night in Parc des Princes.

Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers said on Friday that "the NFL is alert to what's going on".

He added: "This game means a lot to the NFL. If it was unsafe, then I'm sure we wouldn't be here."

A weekend event for Steelers fans was cancelled on Thursday because of security concerns.

articles.title: Lamar Jackson, Puka Nacua, NFL Injury Statuses and Fantasy Impact for Week 7
articles.summary: Lamar Jackson's status for Week 7 is still under evaluation.
articles.body:
Lamar Jackson's status for Week 7 is still under evaluation.

The Baltimore Ravens quarterback, who missed the last two weeks with an ankle injury, was practiced on Friday and said he's improving ahead of Sunday's AFC North battle with the Cincinnati Bengals

Puka Nacua contains a similar status for Sunday after he left Los Angeles Rams practice on Thursday with a calf issue. Nacua didn't suffer a long-term injury, but there are concerns about whether he'll be able to play in Week 7 or not.

Below is a look at all of the significant injury news affecting fantasy football matchups in Week 7.

Lamar Jackson's Status Yet To Be Determined

The Ravens have yet to rule Lamar Jackson out of Sunday's clash with the Cincinnati Bengals.

Jackson, who revealed on Friday that he's been dealing with a high ankle sprain, said he's "heading in the right direction" for Sunday, per ESPN's Jamison Hensley.

Ravens head coach Jesse Minter wouldn't commit either way on Jackson's status when he addressed the media on Friday.

The Ravens posted a 1-1 record without Jackson so far this season. Tyler Huntley led them to an overtime win over the Atlanta Falcons. They then lost to the Cleveland Browns in Week 6.

If Jackson plays, the assumption would be that he doesn't run as much to put more pressure on the ankle. He may be more inclined to sit back in the pocket and throw, or rely more on Derrick Henry to carry the offensive load.

The Bengals allowed over 300 total yards in four of their first five games. They let up over 100 rushing yards in their three games prior to their Week 6 bye.

It's an ideal matchup for Henry, regardless of who the quarterback is, but if Jackson plays, the forecast for the Baltimore pass-catchers is better.

Jackson passed for over 200 yards in three of his four starts. He completed 75 percent of his passes in his last two games before the injury.

Huntley threw for 366 yards in the last two weeks. He was better against Atlanta and struggled a bit against Cleveland in a tougher matchup.

Huntley is a solid replacement for Jackson in fantasy football, if he starts for a third straight week. The matchup against Cincinnati should allow Huntley to put up a similar stat line to the Atlanta game.

Regardless of quarterback, the best waiver-wire move involving a Ravens player is picking up tight end Josh Cuevas. The rookie out of Alabama scored last week and had six catches on seven targets in the last two weeks.

Puka Nacua Listed As Questionable, Does Not Practice Friday

Puka Nacua is officially listed as questionable for the Rams' Week 7 battle with the Las Vegas Raiders.

Nacua left practice on Thursday with a calf issue. That ailment kept him out of practice on Friday.

Nacua's potential absence would be a massive blow to the Rams offense, a unit that is already without Davante Adams for an extended period of time.

Matthew Stafford's fantasy value would crater if Nacua and Adams, arguably the best wide receiver tandem in the NFL, aren't on the field.

Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell and Jordan Whittington are next up on the wide receiver depth chart for the Rams.

However, it might be smarter to go with Blake Corum, Tyler Higbee or Colby Parkinson

The Rams utilize a good amount of multi-tight end sets and they have two solid pass-catching running backs in Corum and Kyren Williams.

The Denver Broncos are a team to target, if you want to pivot away from the Rams as a whole.

Courtland Sutton and Jaylen Waddle haven't had great starts, but they're facing an Arizona Cardinals defense that's given up the second-most touchdowns to wide receivers.

San Francisco's Brandin Cooks is worth a waiver-wire look because of his expanded role in the 49ers offense due to injuries. He's also facing an Atlanta defense that's allowed the most receptions to opposing wide outs.

articles.title: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders Form Union in Historic Move, NFL Team Agrees to Recognize DCCA
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys have agreed to recognize the newly-formed union of their cheerleading squad.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys have agreed to recognize the newly-formed union of their cheerleading squad.

Per a release from the Dallas Cowboy Cheerleaders Association, the NFL organization agreed to recognize the DCCA as the collective bargaining representative for the cheerleading squad.

Schottenheimer 'Pissed Off' by Cowboys Start

The move makes the Dallas Cowboys cheerleaders the first known squad for an NFL team to unionize.

The Cowboys cheerleaders are among the most well-known dance groups in the United States. They have been featured in the Netflix series America's Sweethearts: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders that released its third season in June.

In the second season of the show (h/t Angelique Jackson of Variety ), Megan McElaney revealed in the final episode that a veteran group of the cheerleaders reached out to Cowboys officials to negotiate new contracts.

"We ended up getting a 400% increase, which is, like, life-changing," McElaney said.

McElaney has since retired from the Cowboys cheerleading squad after five seasons.

A 2022 report from Kristen Conti of NBC Sports Boston noted they earn between $15-20 per hour and around $75,000 annually. That amount would have been before the pay increase McElaney spoke about.

The Dallas Cowboys cheerleaders were established in 1961, one year after the team's inaugural season. Their squad is comprised of 36 members with Kelli Finglass serving as director and Judy Tramell serving as choreographer.

articles.title: France's top soccer team obeys police order to move Sunday match; Saints, Steelers owners meet with Macron
articles.summary: Paris Saint-Germain postponed its match under police orders, but the NFL's New Orleans Saints and Pittsburgh Steelers game remains on schedule.
articles.body: It may be starting to get redundant but, "Yes," the NFL game between the New Orleans Saints and Pittsburgh Steelers remains on track, a league spokesman told OutKick and Fox News Digital on Friday. The question came up – again – because the most successful soccer team in France on Friday announced it has postponed its match on Sunday in Paris under police orders. Paris-Saint Germain issued a statement that said it has "taken note" of the order from the Paris Police Prefecture prohibiting the organization of the Paris Saint-Germain-Olympique Lyonnais match. STEELERS CANCEL PARIS FAN EVENT OVER FEARS OF UNREST WHILE NFL PUSHES AHEAD WITH ITS OWN EVENT AND GAME "Accordingly, we inform you that the match between the two clubs, originally scheduled for this Sunday, October 25, has been postponed to Monday, October 26, at 8:30 p.m. at the Parc des Princes," the club said in a statement. The Paris police requested the change because police and security resources are stretched thin due to mass protests, ongoing civil unrest, and France's first NFL game happening in the region, per multiple reports. EXCLUSIVE: SECRETARY OF STATE MARCO RUBIO GIVES NFL COMMISSIONER ASSURANCES THAT GAME IN FRANCE 'WILL BE FINE' That NFL game remains as scheduled on Sunday starting at 9:30 a.m. in the United States. The NFL said so in reply to an email from OutKick and Fox News Digital asking whether and how its decision to play on Sunday is impacted by the decision by PSG. It's not. And that is quite clear considering NFL elites and the French government expect the game to go on. NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell, Saints owner Gayle Benson and Steelers owner Art Rooney II met with French President Emmanuel Macron for a luncheon meeting Friday at the Élysée Palace in Paris. According to a league source, the topics discussed at the two-hour gathering included security for the game, the readiness of the Stade de France, where the game is to be played, and the growth of flag football in France. The fact the French President met with the highest representatives from both squads and there has been no change in the status of the game suggests this thing is going to happen come heck or high rioting. And on that front, it seems Saturday is a key day because protests which may or may not evolve into wider civil unrest are planned for that day. Organizers of the Paris protest told the Associated Press that an administrative court overturned a protest ban issued by police after they challenged it. The Paris prefecture previously said the ban was necessary, given the risk of street violence after groups of masked youth clashed with officers, looted shops and torched cars over the weekend. The organizers signed a police document stating that the protest would remain stationary due to the risk of violence. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! More bans were expected in the coming days. Macron previously said ban measures aim to protect city centers, businesses and public buildings. Macron said after a special security meeting at the Elysée Palace that the strategy adopted for the coming days is to ban protests requested by "individuals or groups with no legitimate authority." "The rules are simple, and I think they’re just common sense. The general recommendation is that there should be no demonstrations in the coming days," he said. "For those who still want to protest, if they are trade unions, prefects will propose alternative routes." Macron blamed last weekend's violence on "actions led by radical far-left groups who aimed to bring the Republic down," in addition to criminals who came to loot. articles.title: President Trump Urges NFL To Postpone Sunday's Steelers-Saints Game
articles.summary: We doubt that happens.
articles.body:
President Donald Trump believes the NFL is playing a dangerous game this Sunday with its international schedule.

The Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints will square off this Sunday at Stade de France in Paris. Although there's plenty of hype surrounding the first-ever NFL game in Paris, fans are worried about all the protests and riots taking place in France's capital.

Paris has been dealing with protests since September as civilians are fed up with poor school conditions as well as the cost of living. Thousands of people have been arrested since the start of these protests. Things have been so bad that a Level II travel advisory was issued for France.

Despite serious safety concerns in Paris, the NFL won't relocate this weekend's game between the Steelers and Saints.

While speaking to the media this Friday afternoon, Trump urged the NFL to postpone the Steelers-Saints game.

"It's looking like tomorrow's going to be a bad day in France, so you worry about it," Trump told reporters. "I would have said the NFL could have probably postponed that match, if you want to know the truth, because France is really in trouble."

Don't expect a change to the NFL schedule.

Peter O'Reilly, the NFL's executive VP of club business, international and league events, said there'll be heightened security measures in place for Sunday's game in Paris.

"There's nothing more important from our standpoint than the teams' security, the fans' security — everybody involved with this game," O'Reilly said at the Fall League Meeting. "Obviously being very vigilant in everything we do, in all of our planning on an hour-by-hour basis, working closely with the two teams."

NFL fans traveling to Paris for this game have received a safety map to ensure they don't end up in harm's way.

We're certainly hoping all the fans, players and coaches safely arrive to Stade de France on Sunday.

articles.title: Knicks' Jalen Brunson Reportedly Will Join Peyton, Eli Manning's 'ManningCast' for Eagles-Cowboys
articles.summary: New York Knicks star Jalen Brunson will be a guest on the ManningCast featuring Peyton and Eli Manning for a Week 7 matchup between the Philadelphia Eagles and Dallas Cowboys, according to Jared Schwartz of the New York Post.
articles.body:
New York Knicks star Jalen Brunson will be a guest on the ManningCast featuring Peyton and Eli Manning for a Week 7 matchup between the Philadelphia Eagles and Dallas Cowboys, according to Jared Schwartz of the New York Post .

Per Schwartz, Brunson is set to make an appearance on ESPN's alternate broadcast during the third quarter of the game.

While the three-time All-Star helped the Knicks end a 53-year championship drought last season, he's a noted Eagles fan.

Brunson was stellar throughout New York's 2026 playoff run, averaging a league-leading 28.4 points per game on 46.5/36.3/84.6 shooting splits. He earned Eastern Conference Finals MVP honors before taking home the Finals MVP award.

As for Monday's NFC East clash, the Eagles and Cowboys are both looking to put slow starts behind them.

Philadelphia sits at just 2-4, as its outlook for the remainder of the year is murky with quarterback Jalen Hurts set to miss the rest of the season due to a blood clot diagnosis.

Dallas similarly owns a 2-4 record, suffering losses in three of its past four games.

Kickoff between the Eagles and Cowboys is on Monday at 8:15 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Fans are sick and tired of the NFL's obsession with flags, anthem fatigue is real & UGA football is too smart!
articles.summary: NFL penalty frustrations and national anthem fatigue dominate fan reactions as the World Series, Brewers, and college football take center stage.
articles.body: 'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news, and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com. We're eight days out, folks. Eight days away from Halloween. Hard to believe, right? October is flying by, and for good reason. We've got a TON going on right now — and that doesn't even include the World Series, which starts tonight. Show of hands ... who's paying attention? I know there's this big debate about small market teams and lack of interest ... blah, blah, blah. RAYS PUNCH THEIR TICKET TO THE WORLD SERIES, TAKING DOWN GUARDIANS IN GAME 6 TO SET UP SERIES WITH BREWERS I don't care. Anything — and I mean anything — beats having to watch the Dodgers. Give me some fresh blood in the Fall Classic. I don't even like the Rays, but I'll take them over the alternative. Obviously, we're all rooting for the Brewers, right? Feels like that's a pretty unanimous choice. If you haven't watched a single second of Brewers baseball this year, do me a favor and watch the first inning tonight. BREWERS' FLAMETHROWER JACOB MISIOROWSKI LIGHTS UP RECORD BOOKS WITH TRIPLE-DIGIT SPEEDS IN GEM VS YANKEES Wait till you see this Jacob Misiorowski pitch. He's gonna blow your minds. On that note, welcome to a Friday Nightcaps — the one where fans (you guys!) weigh in on two things that are pretty top-of-mind at the moment ... Penalties in the NFL, and the ongoing anthem controversies in both the W and NBA. Spoiler alert: You're sick of both! I don't blame you. What else? I've got bedlam in Boone, I thought Kirk Herbstreit was actually really good alongside Al Michaels last night (see, I can be nice!), and let's check in with UGA fans after last week's horrible loss to Auburn. They're doing great! OK, grab you some bologna for National Bologna Day, and settle in for a Friday 'Cap! Frustrated fans, Part I! I'm certain we've celebrated this day before, because I contend that bologna is one of the more — if not the most — underrated meats on the market. People dunk on bologna all the time, and it's baffling to me. I don't get it. I'd put a fried bologna sammy over any sammy in this country. I'm dead serious. It's rare that you can find one anymore, but if you do, you're in for quite a ride. Nice thick slice of bologna? Cheese? Toasted bun. The best. Mount Rushmore of deli meats? Sure! Why not? 1. Bologna (duh) 2. Pepperoni (not sure it counts as a deli meat, but I get it from my Publix deli, so it counts today) 3. Turkey (gotta be sandwich-sliced though. If it's too thin, I walk away. Thinly sliced turkey is for the birds) 4. Roast beef (I had chicken in this spot last year, but I've evolved) And that concludes our culinary portion of today's class! Gordon Ramsay would be proud. OK, let's go ahead and get started by addressing some fan frustration from this past week. First, we'll start with last night's flag-fest in Chicago: Frustrated fans, Part II! Yikes. Look, I don't even think last night was that bad when you compare it to the rest of the year, but still ... the flags in the NFL are out of control right now. I believe Al Michaels made a comment about it last night. Whenever there's a big play, you almost expect a flag. You're STUNNED when you don't see one. That's not a great place to be. There's no flow in these games anymore. No rhythm. It's just a three-hour ref show at this point. I don't know who to blame, by the way. The players? The coaches? The league for, at times, forgetting it's actually tackle football? Everyone probably shares some of it. Bottom line? It's hurting the product. Something has to change. Moving on ... Yesterday, I asked the class how y'all felt about the ongoing anthem debates raging in both the WNBA and with LeBron James. I was curious, mainly because I'm personally just over it all. I don't care anymore. I think it's all silly and the players doing it are insufferable, but I'm just tired of giving them oxygen at this point. It's not worth it. You guys agreed. Here's a quick sampling of some of the responses I received — and I received DOZENS of emails last night. Herbie, Boone & UGA's GPA! Yeah, I cannot stand LeBron James. He's awful, and has been for decades now. He's the worst. But it's 2026. We've known this about LeBron for YEARS now. Why should I let it bother me anymore? What's the point? Why am I letting LEBRON JAMES or the WNBA girls affect my mood? It's silly. I'm over it. Most of you are, too. OK, let's rapid-fire this Friday class into a big weekend of FOOTBALL. First up? I give Herbie and Al Michaels a lot of grief, but I thought Kirk was actually really good last night. He absolutely nailed the most pivotal moment of the game: I was screaming at the TV the second I saw it happen. That play was straight out of the Bill Belichick handbook. I thought it was actually brilliant by Mike Vrabel, and I'm no Mike Vrabel fan. It's the right call. If you somehow stop them, you have to waste a timeout. That's one. They're gonna go for it because Ben Johnson is Ben Johnson. The chances of getting another stop on 4th and inches are very slim. If you don't, the game is basically over because you're only going to have one timeout left and they'll have a new set of downs. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE I'd take my chances with the 58-yard field goal any day of the week in that spot. Good work, Herbie! Less of the dog, and more of THAT! Next? While everyone was watching that Bears-Pats ending, I was dialed in on the App. State-JMU game over in Boone. articles.title: Falcons' throwback logo will not feature stripes from viral social media post
articles.summary: Atlanta's post about its throwback logo drew jokes and criticism about its similarity to Nazi symbolism.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Falcons will take the field Sunday with a throwback logo on their helmets — but not the design that went viral.

As part of their throwback uniforms, the Falcons will bring back a black falcon logo that the team used for more than four decades, starting in the 1960s.

To promote the throwbacks, Atlanta made a social media post showing the design, captioning that it was the team's new profile picture. The post incorporated the throwback logo with a background of red with black, gold and cream stripes, which mimics the striping on the team's retro helmets.

But people online quickly pointed out how the combination of the colors and the black logo evoked the Nazi flag, leading to satirical jokes.

The post is still up on the Falcons' social media, but is no longer the team's profile picture; that change appeared to take place Thursday, after the initial social media reaction. The new profile picture shows a helmet with the retro logo, but without the striping.

The Falcons declined to comment to ESPN about the issue, and the NFL did not respond to a request for comment from the Associated Press .

Atlanta will wear the throwback logos as they host the San Francisco 49ers for Week 7.

articles.title: Give them a C-O-N-T-R-A-C-T: The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders are unionizing
articles.summary: If successful, they'd be the first NFL cheerleading squad to reach a contract.
articles.body:
After years of fighting for better pay and benefits, the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders have unionized.

The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders Association announced Friday that the team has voluntarily recognized the cheerleaders as a collective bargaining unit following a "meaningful discussion." That gives the newly formed union a green light to begin negotiating. If successful, they would be the first NFL cheer squad to reach a contract.

It's another win for football's biggest cheerleading brand, which last year secured a 400 percent raise coming off the massive success of "America's Sweethearts," the Netflix documentary series that put on full display the athleticism and talent it takes to be a competitive NFL cheerleader — and what little pay comes with the job.

The cheerleaders have for years worked together behind the scenes — at one point threatening to stage a walkout — to win higher pay.

During the show's first season, former Cowboys cheerleader Kat Puryear revealed that her salary through 2022 was equivalent to that of "a substitute teacher" or a "Chick-fil-A worker that works full time." That helped jumpstart a conversation that led to all cheerleaders on the team getting a pay bump last year; veterans on the squad went from earning from $15 an hour to $75 an hour.

On the show's second season, Kelli Finglass, the team's director, called the effort to raise wages "60-plus years long overdue."

"Our efforts were heard," Megan McElaney, one of the cheerleaders who led the charge for higher pay, said in the show's final episode. "I get emotional knowing that I was a part of that. Dancers are athletes. They have so much value."

The push by the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders, and now the recognition of their union, marks a sea change for the sport.

In 2014, Lacy Thibodeaux-Fields, then part of the Oakland Raiderettes, sued her team alleging a violation of state minimum wage and labor laws. During the 2014 season, she earned barely $1,000 for work that included nine hours a week in practice, another nine on game days and at least 10 community events per season.

Her case, and several others that came after it, ended in settlements.

For many, the situation has long been symbolic of the gender imbalance that perpetuated years of very little pay for the cheerleaders — lower, even, than what was paid to team mascots . For decades, cheerleading has been cast aside as an "honor" rather than a job that requires skill, training and compensation. But as Thibodeaux-Fields' attorney, Sharon Vinick, pointed out during court proceedings on her case: "It's an honor to be a quarterback, but they don't do it for free."

The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders are the only NFL squad besides the Jills, of the Buffalo Bills, that have tried unionizing. The Jills successfully voted to unionize in 1995, but the effort ultimately dissolved a year later.

The Seattle Seahawks released cornerback Trevon Diggs on Friday, per Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram .

According to Gregg Bell of 93.3 KJR, the Seahawks released Diggs to free up space on their 53-man roster in order for guard Anthony Bradford to come off injured reserve and suit up against the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 7.

The 28-year-old has appeared in three games for the Seahawks this season.

Diggs initially signed with Seattle as a free agent on Aug. 19, although he wasn't able to earn a spot on the team's 53-man roster at the end of training camp. He was retained on the Seahawks' practice squad instead.

On Oct. 10, Seattle signed Diggs off its practice squad ahead of a Week 5 clash with the San Francisco 49ers.

In his three regular-season appearances, he recorded one tackle. He also allowed a 91.7 passer rating when targeted in coverage, according to Pro Football Focus .

Diggs' NFL career started on a high note with the Dallas Cowboys, as he earned Pro Bowl recognition in two consecutive seasons from 2021-22. During his 2021 campaign, he racked up a league-leading 11 interceptions.

Health issues started to impact Diggs, as he suffered a torn ACL in 2023 before missing time during his 2025 season due to a concussion .

While he wasn't able to keep his 53-man roster spot as part of a deep Seahawks secondary, it appears as though he could return to the practice squad of the defending Super Bowl champions.

articles.title: Tom Brady’s $375 million Fox contract and 5% Raiders stake give the NFL legend two major post-retirement plays
articles.summary: Tom Brady earns about $37.5 million a year to talk football. That comes from his 10-year, $375 million contract with Fox.
articles.body: Tom Brady earns about $37.5 million a year to talk football. That comes from his 10-year, $375 million contract with Fox. He also owns roughly 5 percent of the Las Vegas Raiders, a stake NFL owners approved 32-0 in October 2024. The broadcast job started rough. Brady struggled as Fox's lead analyst in year one, then adjusted, and Fox's NFL games averaged 18.7 million viewers in 2025-26, up 6 percent. Both deals come with limits.Tom Brady's $375 million Fox deal pays off after a rough first yearTom Brady used to be paid to take hits. Fox now pays him about $37.5 million a year to sit in a booth, more than the roughly $25 million he made at his playing peak. It is an odd twist for a quarterback whose biggest check arrived after retirement.The first season did not look like a bargain.By his own account, Brady watched his broadcasts and winced. "Why'd I say that?" he'd ask. "I didn't like that. That made no sense." He showed up with pages of notes and read too much of them, a habit he later called too much information. The prep buried the show instead of helping it.So he changed the process. He went back to preparing like a player: scouting matchups, guessing the next move, building a game plan. Year two landed better. Analyst Richard Deitsch said Brady sounded more "competent" and "lucid," and his breakdown of how receivers track deep balls by watching shoulder pads drew praise.His partner Kevin Burkhardt described the dynamic simply. "Tom's the quarterback," he said. "We're trying to be a good teammate and get open on third down for him."Brady is still tinkering. "Even now, I probably have too much information," he said. "I think next year I'm going to streamline it even more."How the Raiders stake limits what Brady can see and sayOwnership came with a fight. Brady and Knighthead Capital co-founder Tom Wagner agreed in May 2023 to buy about 10 percent of the Raiders from Mark Davis, with Brady holding 5 percent. Approval took 17 months. Owners worried Davis had given the pair too big a discount, and some feared a part-owner of one team would pick up inside details on rivals from the broadcast side.The league answered with restrictions.Brady cannot attend production meetings, in person or virtually. He has no access to team facilities, players or coaches. He can call Raiders games, but league rules bar him from publicly criticizing officials or other clubs. He also cannot play again unless he sells.The criticism rule is the one that costs him most. Viewers tune in to a former quarterback for blunt opinions, and Brady has to hold some of them back. Fox is paying for his voice with a few topics fenced off. How well that works will show up in the ratings.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

The San Francisco 49ers will be without receiver Mike Evans, among others, for Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons.

Evans' health is now under the microscope again following Monday's setback.

articles.title: Vance receives warm reception during Bengals visit despite negative media portrayal: source

articles.body: The narrative on social media that Vice President JD Vance was ignored by multiple Cincinnati Bengals players at a recent team practice apparently does not reflect what actually unfolded that day, a source with knowledge of the visit told OutKick. A recent video shared online showed Vance and his family outside the team's locker room on Thursday as the team walked back in. The video, that did not have clear audio of the interaction, showed Bengals tight end Drew Sample stop to shake the vice president's hand as other players walked by. articles.body: In 2020, as the COVID-19 pandemic brought daily life to a standstill, Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen used their resources to help families facing food shortages in Florida. articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys agreed to recognize the newly formed union as the collective bargaining representative for the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders, one of the most famous dance groups in sports — let alone the country — have unionized after their limited pay and benefits have been the subject of discussion and controversy for years.

And their newly formed union is now recognized by the Dallas Cowboys as the collective bargaining representative for the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders.

The union, officially named the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders Association (DCCA), gained that recognition "after meaningful discussion" with the Cowboys, according to a Friday news release from the parties , which states that they are set to start collective bargaining.

During Season 2 of the Netflix docuseries "America's Sweethearts" — one of the multiple television series that have profiled the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders — the dancers' salaries were thrust back into the spotlight.

The cheerleaders said they were due to receive a 400% pay raise for the 2025 season, as reported by The Dallas Morning News .

While the show didn't disclose the new wages, or detail the cheerleaders' previous earnings, Jada McLean told The New York Teams that she was making $15 an hour and $500 for each appearance in 2024, her fifth and final year with the squad (compensation varies by experience, she explained).

After the raise that was revealed in Season 2 of "America's Sweethearts," though, veteran cheerleaders could be reeling in more than $75 an hour, McLean told the Times. That new contract, according to the June 2025 report from the Times , altered the pay structure for game days and other appearances as well, except it still didn't provide health insurance, per McLean.

Back in 2018, Dallas Cowboys Cheerleader Erica Wilkins filed a federal fair wage lawsuit against the Cowboys, whom Forbes values at $17 billion . Wilkins, according to The Guardian , claimed she averaged $15,000 during her seasons and brought in less money than the Cowboys' male mascot.

The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders have been a staple for decades. Their high kicks are iconic, as is their "Thunderstruck" routine.

The group surged in popularity among a new generation of fans when Netflix debuted "America's Sweethearts" in 2024. There have now been three seasons of that show.

Time will tell if, or how much, impending collective bargaining between DCCA and the Cowboys will improve the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders' compensation.

It's worth noting that, in 1995, the Buffalo Bills' cheerleaders won a National Labor Relations Board ruling that allowed them to unionize, per the Associated Press via the Los Angeles Times . It was also reported at the time that the group, the Buffalo Jills, then joined the National Football League Cheerleaders Association.

That was reportedly the first union to represent a professional cheerleading squad. The union didn't last, however, and the Jills suspended operations in 2014 in the wake of a lawsuit filed by former cheerleaders who, per ESPN , claimed they were underpaid and mistreated.

New York Giants linebacker Tremaine Edmunds will miss the remainder of the 2026 season with a shoulder injury, The Athletic's Dan Duggan reports .

Edmunds was already listed as out for Week 7's matchup with the Houston Texans. However, he is apparently dealing with a torn muscle extending to his chest, according to ESPN's Jordan Ranaan .

The injury occurred late in the Giants' 34-27 win over the New Orleans Saints in Week 6. Reaching with his left arm attempting to tackle Saints running back Kendre Miller, Edmunds stayed down on the field after the play.

Edmunds, 28, was in his first season with the Giants. He signed a three-year, $36 million deal in March, days after the Chicago Bears released him to create $15 million in salary cap space.

In six games, Edmunds compiled 50 total tackles with 2 sacks and 3 tackles for loss as the Giants' defensive playcaller. He appeared to be on his way to a ninth consecutive season recording 100 or more tackles, averaging 129 per year.

Edmunds was a Pro Bowl selection in 2019 and 2020 with the Buffalo Bills, who made him their 2018 first-round pick (No. 16 overall) out of Virginia Tech.

Micah McFadden is expected to replace Edmunds at one of the Giants' inside linebacker spots alongside rookie (and first-round pick) Arvell Reese. McFadden, 26, has appeared in five games this season, recording 4 tackles. He started at inside linebacker in 2023 and 2024, averaging 104 tackles per season.

Edmunds' injury further erodes the Giants' depth at linebacker. Edge rusher Chauncey Golsteon will also miss the remainder of the season with a neck injury. Fellow edge Brian Burns tore his ACL in Week 3's 12-7 win over the Tennessee Titans.

articles.title: Trump says NFL 'could've probably postponed' Paris game as France protests stretch police thin
articles.summary: President Donald Trump says the NFL could have postponed the Steelers-Saints Paris game as mass protests stretch police and security resources.
articles.body: President Donald Trump is skeptical about the National Football League continuing to hold its first-ever game in Paris amid protests. The Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints are still set to kick off Sunday despite the civil unrest and a Paris Saint-Germain soccer game the same day being postponed. Paris police requested a postponement of the PSG game because police and security resources are stretched thin due to mass protests, ongoing civil unrest and France's first NFL game happening in the region, per multiple reports. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE The NFL said in a reply to an email from OutKick and Fox News Digital that the PSG game did not impact any potential decision to move the Steelers-Saints game. However, Trump said the NFL "could've probably postponed that match." "It's looking like tomorrow is going to be a bad day in France, so you worry about it. I would've said the NFL could've probably postponed that match... France is really in trouble," Trump told reporters on Friday. Trump then took a shot at Democratic policies. "That's what happens when you go left. That's what happens when you allow unlimited numbers of people into your country from very unfriendly countries." The NFL has insisted multiple times this week that Sunday's game in France will be safe to play and safe for fans to attend amid civil unrest. However, the Steelers canceled a fan event in the area. According to a league source, the topics discussed at the two-hour gathering included security for the game, the readiness of the Stade de France, where the game is to be played and the growth of flag football in France. Organizers of the Paris protest told the Associated Press that an administrative court overturned a protest ban issued by police after they challenged it. The Paris prefecture previously said the ban was necessary, given the risk of street violence after groups of masked youth clashed with officers, looted shops and torched cars over the weekend. VANCE RECEIVES WARM RECEPTION DURING BENGALS VISIT DESPITE NEGATIVE MEDIA PORTRAYAL: SOURCE The organizers signed a police document stating that the protest would remain stationary due to the risk of violence. Earlier this week, Dani Watt, the wife of Steelers defensive end TJ Watt, questioned publicly why the game has not been moved. "Tell me how this one makes sense???" Watt posted. The NFL on Thursday told OutKick that its own NFL Fan House event scheduled for Friday and Saturday remains as scheduled. "It's happening," a league spokesman said. On Wednesday, NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell said he would attend the game and had spoken with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio in recent days about moving forward with it. Rubio told OutKick that the American embassy in France believes the game "will be fine." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP OutKick's Armando Salguero contributed to this report.

articles.title: Sam LaPorta Feels 'Bad' If Honest Quotes on Lions Contract Were Distraction, Clarifies Intentions
articles.summary: Detroit Lions tight end Sam LaPorta didn't want his comments about contract talks with the team to become a distraction.
articles.body:
Detroit Lions tight end Sam LaPorta didn't want his comments about contract talks with the team to become a distraction.

Speaking to reporters on Friday, LaPorta said he feels "bad" if he caused a distraction for the Lions and clarified what he was trying to say.

"I feel bad if there was any sort of distraction to the team or my teammates or the coaches, but I think there was maybe a misconception with… My intentions are I want to play for this team," LaPorta said. "I give everything I have. My teammates do, as well. They all love me, respect me and support me, and they want to see me be happy and be compensated."

LaPorta made headlines earlier this week during an appearance on Pardon My Take when discussing his future. He said the Lions were "not showing the love" and hinted at potentially playing elsewhere when his rookie deal expires after this season.

"I'm going to continue to do my thing and ball out, and in three months, if I don't get to wear the Honolulu blue and play for the Lions anymore, it's going to be all good. I'll go get paid somewhere else," LaPorta said (h/t ESPN.com ). "So whatever."

Later in the podcast, LaPorta referenced the season-ending back injury he suffered last year as part of what he has given to the Lions organization without feeling like it is reciprocated:

"I think the combination of getting your heartstrings twisted as well as the violent sport that we play, it sucks. It's disappointing that you go out there every week and you bear the risk of getting hurt. Like last year, whatever it was, Week 9, Week 10, I break my f--king back for the team. And then I'm going out there this year and I'm balling, and maybe they're just not showing the love."

Lions head coach Dan Campbell downplayed the situation when discussing it during his Friday press conference, saying he didn't "even think twice about those comments because I know what he's about."

Detroit does not currently have a tight end under contract beyond the 2026 season. LaPorta, Brock Wright and Tyler Conklin are all set to become free agents.

A second-round pick in the 2023 NFL draft, LaPorta is making $5.7 million this season. Last year marked the first time he suffered a major injury after appearing in 33 out of 34 games between the 2023 and '24 seasons.

LaPorta has played in each of Detroit's first five games so far this season. He ranks second on the team with 316 receiving yards and three receiving touchdowns.

Her words highlighted the human side of the NFL's Crucial Catch campaign, which promotes cancer awareness and early detection. articles.title: “So you see a lot of that inequality”: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders unionize after years of pay disputes as collective bargaining begins
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders have taken a major step in their fight for better pay.
articles.body: The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders have taken a major step in their fight for better pay. Recently, the Cowboys agreed to recognize the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders Association as the squad’s collective bargaining representative. The decision gives the cheerleaders a formal voice in negotiations with the NFL franchise after years of debate over their compensation.The move comes after the Netflix series America’s Sweethearts: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders brought their working lives and financial struggles to a wider audience. While the squad received a major pay increase in 2025, union recognition opens a new chapter in its push for better workplace terms. Dallas Cowboys recognize cheerleaders’ union after years of pay concernsThe Cowboys and the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders Association announced the agreement in a joint statement on Friday. The statement praised the squad’s talent and dedication and described the cheerleaders as an important part of the organization.The recognition clears the way for collective bargaining, which allows representatives to negotiate employment terms on behalf of the group. However, the announcement did not outline a new pay deal or confirm specific benefits. Those details will depend on negotiations between the two sides.The development follows years of scrutiny over cheerleader compensation. In 2018, former Cowboys cheerleader Erica Wilkins filed a lawsuit over her pay. The case ended in a 2019 settlement that doubled the squad’s per-game pay from $200 to $400.That increase marked a significant change, but it did not end questions about how much cheerleaders earned for their work. Their responsibilities extend beyond performing during NFL games, with rehearsals, appearances and other duties also demanding time and effort.Virginia Commonwealth University professor Victor Chen, who studies labor issues as a sociologist said that Dallas Cowboys cheerleaders were likely helped by having such a high profile and the Netflix show.He also said that without that the team may have just tried to replace the cheerleaders because there are many people who would take jobs in the entertainment industry at low pay“So you see a lot of that inequality of compensation in any sort of artistic or entertainment field where you have lots of people clamoring to get into it and maybe being unpaid or very poorly paid to do so,” Chen said.Netflix series put Dallas Cowboys cheerleaders’ pay fight in spotlightThe second season of Netflix’s America’s Sweethearts: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders, which aired in 2025, brought fresh attention to the squad’s pay negotiations.During the series, a cheerleader said members had received a 400% pay increase. The raise followed negotiations over compensation and represented another major jump after the 2019 settlement.Reports surrounding the 2025 increase highlighted how sharply cheerleader pay had changed over several years. Still, the raise and the newly recognized union represent two separate developments. The earlier increase improved compensation, while union recognition creates a formal structure for future negotiations.The Cowboys are one of the most valuable franchises in professional sports, according to Forbes. Their cheerleaders also enjoy international recognition, strengthened by decades of performances and the Netflix series. Yet the squad’s popularity has not removed questions about compensation and working conditions.The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders are not the first NFL cheerleading squad to pursue union representation. The Buffalo Jills, who cheered for the Buffalo Bills, won the right to unionize in 1995. The squad later disbanded after a 2014 lawsuit raised allegations involving unpaid work and sexual harassment.After years of pay disputes and a major increase in 2025, the cheerleaders now have a formal route to negotiate their employment terms. What comes out of those talks will determine how much the union changes their working lives.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: “Incredibly Demeaning”: Ex-Chiefs Star Slams Dan Orlovsky for Claiming Patrick Mahomes Secretly Directs Kenneth Walker
articles.summary: Former Chiefs star Mitchell Schwartz did not like what he heard about Kenneth Walker on ESPN’s NFL Live. Dan Orlovsky said Patrick Mahomes appears to give th...
articles.body:
Former Chiefs star Mitchell Schwartz did not like what he heard about Kenneth Walker on ESPN's NFL Live. Dan Orlovsky said Patrick Mahomes appears to give the running back hand signals about the run game, and Schwartz fired back on X:

"This feels incredibly demeaning to Kenneth Walker that you think he needs to be told what a simple 4 down front is and how that's going to be blocked. And what a Bear front is, etc. Like he doesn't know how to read basic defensive fronts and find the DL he's supposed to key."

Schwartz was reacting to a clip Orlovsky shared himself. In the post, Orlovsky wrote that Mahomes was "secretly" telling Walker the run game calls and called it "very cool." In the video, he made sure Chiefs fans did not see it as a weakness:

"There's definitely some communication non-verbally that Patrick's giving Kenneth Walker when it comes to the run game. And just for Chiefs fans, this isn't something that's going to make you predictable, or teams are going to be able to steal it."

Orlovsky then walked through the frames. He said Mahomes' left hand looked like a fist against a four-man front, which he read as a sign that the run should stay front-side with a double team. Later, he said Mahomes held out one finger against a five-man front, which Orlovsky believed Mahomes used to indicate "five guys."

"I think those hand signals are a way where Patrick is communicating to Kenneth Walker, 'This is what the run game blocking is, code-wise or call side,' and it's giving him an advantage of what to expect when it comes to those blocks."

That is where Schwartz drew the line. He spent years blocking in the same trenches and was able to point out that this was nothing out of the ordinary. Schwartz won a Super Bowl with the Chiefs.

It also helps to know how good Walker has been. Orlovsky said on The Pat McAfee Show earlier this week that Walker deserved MVP over Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen, and the numbers back up the buzz. Through five games, Walker has an NFL-high 665 rushing yards on 106 carries, 6.3 yards per carry, and eight total touchdowns.

Walker set the stage with 173 yards and a touchdown against the Denver Broncos in September. The game also marked Mahomes' return from his ACL and LCL tears.

The two do work closely on the field, though that does not confirm what Orlovsky described. Kenneth Walker has said Mahomes usually spots the cutback before he does. In the Chiefs' 22-6 win over the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 6, Mahomes even threw a block that helped spring a red-zone touchdown run, and he explained why Walker keeps him on his toes.

Walker is putting forward a season for the books. This season, he's already recorded four 100+ rushing-yard games. He caused some serious damage in the Raiders game, rushing for a season-high 177 yards.

Walker's prowess is already established by the tape. He doesn't really need help sneaked in to make all these big plays. Walker has already won the Super Bowl MVP last season with the Seattle Seahawks , rushing for 135 yards in that game.

Patrick Mahomes, ever the team player, is also looking out for his star RB for their upcoming matchup against the Seahawks.

"I know it's going to be a special moment for him…," the QB said. "You get to go back to a place where you built your career and won a Super Bowl… at the end of the day, you've got to win a football game… He knows we've got his back."

articles.title: Kenneth Walker III returns to haunt Seattle Seahawks, J.J. McCarthy time in New York and Los Angeles Rams pressure - NFL Gameday Guide
articles.summary: Watch the Pittsburgh Steelers face the New Orleans Saints in the first-ever regular-season game in Paris, France from 1pm, live on Sky Sports NFL; Kenneth Walker then returns with the Kansas City Chiefs to face his former team after inspiring the Seattle Seahawks to Super Bowl glory
articles.body:
Kenneth Walker III returns to Seattle for the first time since his blockbuster exit this Sunday as he leads out the Kansas City Chiefs against the same Seahawks team he inspired to Super Bowl glory back in February.

The running back posted 135 yards on the ground as Mike Macdonald's side beat the New England Patriots at the NFL's showpiece climax in Santa Clara. But instead of extending the Super Bowl MVP, Seattle allowed Walker to hit free agency, where he would sign a three-year $45m deal with the Chiefs as their marquee needle-shoving offseason addition.

Behind Walker Patrick Mahomes' refurbished, reinvigorated dynasty Chiefs are back in Super Bowl contention; he has changed the game entirely for Andy Reid. Next in line - his old flame.

"It's going to be a special moment for him," said Chiefs quarterback Mahomes. "You get to go back to the place where you built your career, where you won a Super Bowl. "Those fans are the people that were around him for all of that. Those are a still a lot of the guys that were his teammates, that he grew up with as well in the NFL.

"At the end of the day, you've got to win a football game. He knows we have his back."

A merry Seahawks GM John Schneider joked during his side's Super Bowl parade of how Walker had tried to negotiate a new deal with him five minutes earlier, describing the moment as 'weird'. What was instead weirder was the decision not to extend a defining figure in Seattle's Lombardi surge.

Still, it would become a broken Chiefs team's transformative gain, Walker having since provided an MVP-calibre impact to an offense that had lost all identity, all spark, all pizzazz in recent years.

Walker leads the NFL with 665 rushing yards at 6.3 yards per carry through six weeks, while averaging a league-most 133 yards on the ground per game and having scored a tied-second-most eight touchdowns from scrimmage. His 760 scrimmage yards are second only to Bijan Robinson, and no back has broken more tackles or averaged more yards after contact per carry than Walker.

In doing so he has dictated a heightened respect for the Chiefs' activity out of the backfield, coupled with the scrambling ability of Mahomes. His immediate threat has unleashed Kansas City's play-action game, and so too Mahomes' freedom to stretch the field with the deep-shot aggression and three-level concepts that have been largely non-existent in the last couple of seasons. It is a Chiefs offense reborn, and Walker has been at the heart of change.

"If you have one weak link in the chain, the great running backs will find that. Ken will do that, and he has the past bunch of games this season," said Seahawks safety Julian Love.

While the Chiefs rank second in rushing offense, the Seahawks lie down in 18th with an average of 107.2 yards per game as they await the return of Zach Charbonnet, who was activated off the PUP list this week.

Charbonnet had been Seattle's starting running back over Walker before tearing his ACL in the playoffs, during which the latter recorded 65 carries for 313 yards and four touchdowns alongside nine catches for 104 yards.

The Chiefs have long yearned for another superstar face on offense with which to support Mahomes, particularly coming into his first season since last December's year-ending knee injury. Walker has lived up to the billing and more, inspiring the return of Mahomes magic by becoming the face of Andy Reid's attack. Few saw it going quite this well.

The Seahawks chose not to pay him. Pay for it, they might.

The NFL is primed to make more history on Sunday when the New Orleans Saints host the Pittsburgh Steelers in the first-ever regular-season game to be played in Paris, France.

The iconic Stade de France opens its doors as the newest host stadium to football, with Paris featuring among a record nine international games being played during the 2026 campaign and joining Melbourne and Rio de Janeiro as a brand new territory for the league.

Civil unrest around the city has dominated much of this week's build-up to the game, however the NFL remain in constant communication with French authorities and insist they do not expect Sunday's game to be disrupted. Aaron Rodgers' Steelers enter the contest 4-2 following last Sunday's overtime victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, while the Saints are 2-4 coming off their win at the New York Giants.

More change awaits at quarterback for the Giants as J.J. McCarthy prepares to make his first start under center against the Houston Texans, taking the reins from Jameis Winston in the wake of last weekend's impressive cameo against the Saints.

McCarthy threatened an unlikely Giants comeback when entered the game while trailing by 24 in the fourth quarter before throwing for 243 yards, the most-ever across an 11-minute span in NFL history. It has prompted John Harbaugh to go and find out what he has (or doesn't have) in the former first-round pick, who arrived via a trade from the Minnesota Vikings following the season-ending injury to Jaxson Dart.

McCarthy's NFL career has stuttered since he entered the league as the 10th overall pick in 2024, injury in his rookie preseason opening the door for Sam Darnold's career-resurrection before a combination of poor play, more injuries and the eventual arrival of Kyler Murray would spell the end in Minnesota. Now, is his chance. With a Malik Nabers-sized talisman at his disposal.

The NFL has its share of elite wide receiver tandems, from Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins to CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens to Puka Nacua and Davante Adams.

Frightening tight end tandems are a little less common, but the Las Vegas Raiders have forged one of their own. Brock Bowers rightly gets the acclaim as Klint Kubiak's prized weapon on offense - looking every bit a wide receiver in a tight end's body - but it is also becoming something of a breakout year for teammate Michael Mayer.

The 2023 second-round pick has 28 catches for 266 yards and a touchdown through six games as a prominent target alongside Bowers and Tre Tucker, his 162 yards after catch ranked fourth among tight ends. As teams game-plan to contain Bowers, Mayer's value is beginning to show.

His Raiders sit 3-3 as they take on the struggling Los Angeles Rams, who face mounting scrutiny after a 2-4 start at the bottom of the NFC West. Sean McVay's team purred into the year widely recognised as Super Bowl favourites courtesy of a Myles Garrett acquisition, an Aaron Donald return, an MVP-winning Matthew Stafford and the lasting memory of their narrow NFC Championship Game loss to the Seattle Seahawks.

Marquee injuries have combined with a special teams mess in leaving them playing catch-up in one of football's toughest divisions. It wasn't supposed to go like this.

Xavier McKinney may warrant more attention as Green Bay's All-Pro safety, but Evan Williams is emerging as one of Matt LaFleur's unsung stars on defense. The 2024 fourth-round pick is Pro Football Focus's highest-graded safety through six weeks of the season, his influence going beyond mere statistics as one of the most intelligent and versatile players in his position across the league.

His ground coverage, play diagnosis, elite instincts and ball skills were demonstrated last week as he retreated from the line of scrimmage post-snap before gliding across to pick off Dak Prescott in the red zone of his side's win over the Dallas Cowboys.

He has become an instrumental part of Jonathan Gannon's Packers defense, which ranks eighth in yards allowed this season ahead of Sunday's rivalry match with the Detroit Lions.

As for the Lions, tight end Sam LaPorta faces some added attention in light of comments made during the week criticising the Lions for their approach to a prospective new deal. LaPorta, in the final season of his rookie contract, insisted he will "get paid somewhere else" should he and the team not find a resolution over his extension.

"I think the combination of getting your heartstrings twisted as well as the violent sport that we play, it sucks," LaPorta said on Barstool's "Pardon My Take" podcast. "It's disappointing that you go out there every week and you bear the risk of getting hurt. "Like last year, whatever it was, Week Nine, Week 10, I break my f****** back for the team. And then I'm going out there this year and I'm balling, and maybe they're just not showing the love."

This is the CJ Stroud the NFL knew and loved during his standout rookie season.

The CJ Stroud NFL disciples forecast to join the league's elite quarterbacks, and the CJ Stroud capable of leading this Texans team to Super Bowl contention.

DeMeco Ryans endorsed his fanbase's MVP clamour surrounding Stroud last week after watching his quarterback star in Houston's win over the Jacksonville Jaguars at Wembley Stadium. He finished the game 24 of 34 passing for 312 yards, three touchdowns and his first interception of the year, among his highlights a stunning deep-shot to Jaylin Noel with pressure in his face.

Stroud ranks third in passing yards with 1,714 for nine touchdowns to just one pick, his 285.7 yards per game good for fourth in the league. He is on a heater.

articles.title: Falcons vs. 49ers: 4 key matchups to watch in Week 7
articles.summary: Breaking down 4 key matchups to watch in Sunday's Falcons-49ers game
articles.body:
Only the Minnesota Vikings have a more-difficult schedule remaining this season than the Atlanta Falcons . The brutality begins on Sunday afternoon when they host the undefeated San Francisco 49ers, who are widely considered the best team in the NFL right now.

Here are four key matchups the Falcons will have to win if they stand any chance at an upset.

Offensive coordinator Tommy Rees has one of the most-challenging assignments this week as he has to match wits with former Falcons head coach Raheem Morris, who is now calling defensive plays for the 49ers. Atlanta has a roughly-average offense in terms of scoring and yardage, while the Niners rank fifth in fewest yards allowed per game and fourth in scoring defense so far this season.

For the Falcons offense to run right it has to go through running back Bijan Robinson, not quarterback Michael Penix. That's been a problem the last two weeks. Now Atlanta has to get Robinson going despite facing the best off-ball linebacker on the planet. Fred Warner ranks third in the league in tackles this year and his 92.2 PFF grade against the run is the best in the game at his position. Meanwhile, Robinson ranks second in rushing yards and has the highest rushing grade (90.9) among running backs.

Atlanta may have to go without defensive centerpiece Divine Deablo this week, as he's dealing with a bicep injury. That puts more pressure on the Falcons' rookie linebackers, starting with Kendal Daniels. He has the unenviable task of keeping up with the best tight end in the NFL, George Kittle - who leads the Niners with five touchdown catches this season to go with 337 yards. articles.title: Rhamondre Stevenson says Bears' defensive alignment helped with 48-yard TD
articles.summary: Patriots running back Rhamondre Stevenson made one of the most stunning plays of this NFL season when he turned a short pass at the end of the first half and...
articles.body:
Patriots running back Rhamondre Stevenson made one of the most stunning plays of this NFL season when he turned a short pass at the end of the first half and ran for a 48-yard touchdown against the Bears. Stevenson said the Bears' defensive alignment made it possible.

The Bears were so concerned about giving up a Hail Mary on the last play of the half that they put two defensive backs near the goal line, almost 50 yards downfield. The Bears also rushed six to try to prevent Patriots quarterback Drake Maye from having time to set up for a Hail Mary. But that meant the middle of the field was wide open.

"It's kind of how they lined up pre-snap that got us into that play," Stevenson said.

The Bears' defense seemed to be caught off-guard, not expecting Maye to dump it off to Stevenson only a yard past the line of scrimmage. And it's not surprising the Bears weren't expecting it, as scoring a touchdown in that situation is almost unheard of: According to Doug Clawson of CBS Sports, there have been 1,006 plays in the last 20 years in the final 10 seconds of a half, starting more than 40 yards from the end zone, in which the ball was thrown less than 10 yards downfield, and Stevenson's catch was the only one of those 1,006 plays that turned into a touchdown.

"I was just trying to make a play, put my team in a position to swing the game a little bit, as much as we can," Stevenson said. "We've been working on that play for a long time and it came in handy today. Executed on that play so it felt good to do that."

Asked what his mindset was when Maye threw him the Ball, Stevenson answered, "Score."

He did that, producing one of the best touchdowns of this NFL season.
