articles.title: Kansas City Chiefs make history after Week 6 with major franchise milestone
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs made franchise history after their 22-6 victory over the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 6. Nick Bolton set a new team record for games w...
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs left Week 6 with more than another victory. Their 22-6 win over the Los Angeles Chargers on Oct. 18, 2026, kept them unbeaten at 5-0 and delivered a historic achievement for linebacker Nick Bolton.

Bolton recorded 11 tackles against Los Angeles, giving him 26 career games with at least 10 tackles and moving him past Derrick Johnson for the most such games in franchise history. The milestone highlighted the Chiefs' defensive strength during an impressive start to the season.

Quarterback Patrick Mahomes also reached 100 regular-season wins as a starter, matching Tom Brady for the fewest starts needed to reach that mark. With Kenneth Walker III adding 128 rushing yards and 2 touchdowns, Kansas City had several reasons to celebrate as it prepared for its next challenge.

Nick Bolton claims a place in Chiefs history

Bolton recorded 11 tackles against Los Angeles, bringing his career total of games with at least 10 tackles to 26. That moved him past former Chiefs linebacker Derrick Johnson, who previously held the franchise mark.

The achievement reflects Bolton's steady presence in the middle of Kansas City's defense. Double-digit tackle performances require consistent involvement, and the linebacker has built a reputation as a dependable contributor since entering the NFL.

Bolton's record came during a game in which the Chiefs defense repeatedly disrupted the Chargers. Kansas City registered four sacks, forced two takeaways and stopped Los Angeles from reaching the end zone, helping secure the team's fifth victory.

Patrick Mahomes reaches 100 regular-season wins

Mahomes also reached a major career milestone against the Chargers, earning his 100th regular-season win as a starting quarterback. He achieved the mark in his 131st start, matching Tom Brady for the fewest starts needed to reach 100 wins.

The quarterback completed 23 of 30 passes for 272 yards. Although he threw an interception, Kansas City controlled the game for much of the afternoon and built a 19-3 halftime lead before adding a fourth-quarter field goal.

Mahomes' milestone adds to his already remarkable résumé, but the Chiefs' immediate priority remains winning games. His experience and ability to manage difficult stretches continue to matter as Kansas City pursues another deep postseason run.

Kansas City improved to 5-0 through Week 6, making it the only undefeated team in the AFC at that point. The team had also enjoyed a Week 5 bye, meaning its perfect record extended across five games.

The start marked the third time the Chiefs had opened 5-0 under head coach Andy Reid and Mahomes. According to the team, that coach-quarterback combination became only the fourth in league history to achieve the feat.

An unbeaten record does not guarantee a championship, particularly with most of the regular season still ahead. However, Kansas City's early consistency gives it a strong foundation while its coaches continue refining the offense and defense.

Running back Kenneth Walker III delivered one of the game's defining performances, rushing for 128 yards and 2 touchdowns on 19 carries. His explosive runs helped Kansas City establish control early and maintain separation from Los Angeles.

Walker scored on a 33-yard run in the first quarter, then added a 2-yard touchdown before halftime. His second score helped extend the lead, and Harrison Butker's 50-yard field goal just before the break made it 19-3.

Walker's production has been a major part of Kansas City's early success. The Chiefs' official Week 6 recap reported that he had reached at least 100 rushing yards in 4 of the team's first 5 games, giving the offense a reliable ground threat alongside Mahomes.

Kansas City's defense delivers a statement

The defense made the Chargers work for every opportunity. Kansas City sacked quarterback Justin Herbert 4 times, ending a three-game stretch without a sack and turning its pressure into tangible results.

The Chiefs also forced 2 takeaways. Linebacker Jack Cochrane intercepted Herbert in the second quarter, while a fourth-quarter fumble forced by cornerback L'Jarius Sneed was recovered by linebacker Drue Tranquill.

Los Angeles managed just 6 points, all from field goals, despite reaching the Kansas City 1-yard line early in the second half. A holding penalty stalled that drive, and the Chargers settled for 3 points instead of a touchdown.

The AFC West remains within Kansas City's control

The victory moved Kansas City to 3-0 against AFC West opponents. Winning division games is especially valuable because those results can influence the standings and potential playoff positioning later in the season.

The Chiefs have also enjoyed sustained success against their division rivals in recent years. The team's official recap noted that Kansas City held a 39-12 record against the AFC West since 2018, the best mark against a team's own division over that span.

Still, the division race is far from settled. The Chiefs must continue performing against familiar opponents while navigating a demanding schedule, and every future divisional matchup will provide another test of their consistency.

Kansas City's next scheduled matchup is a road game against the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday, Oct. 25. The prime-time contest will offer the Chiefs another opportunity to protect their unbeaten record away from home.

The team will look to carry its defensive momentum into Seattle while maintaining the balance that has helped its offense succeed. Walker's running production, Mahomes' passing and the defense's improved pressure all remain key elements to watch.

The result will not erase the importance of the milestones already reached, but it could shape the conversation around Kansas City's early-season form. A sixth consecutive win would strengthen the Chiefs' position as the season moves deeper into the schedule.

Fun fact: Travis Kelce became the 7th player in NFL history to reach 1,100 career regular-season receptions during the Chiefs' Week 6 win over the Chargers.

The Chiefs are scheduled to visit the Seattle Seahawks on Oct. 25.

Week 7 got underway with Thursday night's battle between the Chicago Bears and New England Patriots. Unfortunately, the game featured another significant injury, as Bears tight end Cole Kmet suffered a knee injury that is expected to end his season.

Several other fantasy stars are on the injury list, too, which will leave many looking to the waiver wire for the rest of the weekend. Additionally, the Buffalo Bills, Jacksonville Jaguars, Los Angeles Chargers, and Washington Commanders will be off this weekend and on bye.

Fortunately, some potential fill-in targets should still be available on the wire heading into the remaining Week 7 schedule.

Here, we'll dive into the Week 7 injury report , provide rankings for the top remaining point-per-reception (PPR) plays, and highlight sleepers who might still be available in your league.

Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson could return from his ankle injury, though he's officially listed as questionable. Baker Mayfield is also questionable but appears set to make his return from a thumb injury and start for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers this week.

"It felt good for him, so it looks like he's ready to go," Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles said of Mayfield, per ESPN's Jenna Laine .

Managers looking to pick up Mayfield will find him available in roughly 60 percent of fantasy leagues. Managers desperate to add a starter late in the week can also consider Eagles backup-turned-starter Tanner McKee.

With Jalen Hurts out for the season with blood clots, McKee will be Philly's starter for the foreseeable future. He got the start last week and delivered just 12.6 fantasy points against the Carolina Panthers. However, McKee has a much more favorable matchup this week against the Dallas Cowboys.

Dallas has surrendered the fifth-most fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks this season.

McKee is rostered in only five percent of fantasy leagues. Aaron Rodgers, J.J. McCarthy, and Geno Smith are other QBs to consider off the wire this week.

Christian McCaffrey, San Francisco 49ers

David Montgomery and Jeremiyah Love are set to miss Week 7 for the Houston Texans and Arizona Cardinals, respectively. The Falcons won't have backup Brian Robinson Jr.

Zach Charbonnet is not quite ready to return for the Seattle Seahawks. However, he should have some long-term value beyond Week 7 and is only rostered in 65 percent of leagues.

The list of running backs who are questionable includes Breece Hall, Rico Dowdle, Jordan Mason, Dylan Sampson, Jonah Coleman, and Mike Washington Jr.

New Orleans Saints running back Alvin Kamara is again questionable with the lingering back injury that has affected him for multiple weeks. This potentially opens the door for Kendre Miller to see substantial workload for a second straight week.

Miller led the Saints with 20 carries and 70 rushing yards against the New York Giants last week. He also added a pair of receptions.

This week, the Saints will battle the Pittsburgh Steelers in the NFL's latest international game. It's not an ideal situation, as the Saints have struggled to run block effectively, and the Steelers are average against the run (14th-fewest fantasy points to opposing RBs).

However, managers won't find many running backs who can get a starter's workload this late in the week. Miller is rostered in 30 percent of leagues. Washington, Samaje Perine, and Jawhar Johnson are other RBs to consider.

While the Buccaneers should have Mayfield this week, they won't have receiver Emeka Egbuka. With him out, Ted Hurst III has some deep sleeper value. He had three catches for 40 yards last week and is rostered in just four percent of fantasy leagues.

The San Francisco 49ers will be short on receivers this week, as both Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel have been ruled out. However, Christian Kirk is questionable and could make his 2026 debut for San Francisco. He's rostered in just 10 percent of leagues.

Rashee Rice will miss a second straight game for the Kansas City Chiefs.

Jets rookie receiver Omar Cooper Jr. is another high-upside target, though he doesn't have the most favorable of Week 7 matchups. New York will host the Miami Dolphins, who have surrendered the third-fewest fantasy points to opposing receivers.

However, Cooper returned from his ankle injury in Week 6 to drop 19.3 fantasy points, and he should be locked into the Jets' No. 2 role moving forward. He's rostered in only 36 percent of fantasy leagues.

Germie Barnard, Jaylin Noel, Keenan Allen, and Tre Tucker are other receivers to consider targeting this week.

The injury report doesn't feature an extensive list of tight ends, though one of the injuries is a big one. Indianapolis Colts star Tyler Warren has been ruled out for the second straight week with a groin injury.

New York Giants tight end Theo Johnson is questionable.

With Davante Adams expected to miss an extended period with his hamstring injury, and with Nacua at less than 100 percent, Los Angeles Rams tight end Tyler Higbee could jump into a huge offensive role. He delivered just 4.2 fantasy points last week but reached double digits in each of his previous games.

This week, the Rams will battle the Las Vegas Raiders, who have surrendered the sixth-most fantasy points (tied) to opposing tight ends this season. Higbee is only rostered in 21 percent of fantasy leagues.

T.J. Hockenson and Pat Freiermuth are two other tight ends who may be found on the wire and who have legitimate sleeper potential in Week 7.

articles.title: Is Jason Kelce about to make a stunning Eagles coaching move? Former NFL star breaks silence amid offensive line crisis
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles could use the wisdom of a former star as their offensive line battles injuries and inconsistency, but Jason Kelce is not ready to
articles.body: The Philadelphia Eagles could use the wisdom of a former star as their offensive line battles injuries and inconsistency, but Jason Kelce is not ready to return to the team in a coaching capacity. The retired center has made his position clear, citing a demanding schedule and the availability of more experienced coaches. His decision comes during a major transition in Philadelphia, where the departure of longtime offensive line coach Jeff Stoutland has left the team adjusting to a new era. Despite his deep connection to the franchise, Kelce believes helping from the sidelines is one thing, while committing to an NFL coaching job is another.Jason Kelce explains why he will not coach the EaglesPhiladelphia's offensive line has faced a difficult start to the 2026 season. Injuries have sidelined three starting linemen, while the team has struggled to establish its running game and protect quarterback Jalen Hurts. New offensive line coach Chris Kuper now faces the challenge of rebuilding consistency in a unit that once stood among the team's strengths.Naturally, Kelce's name has entered the conversation. The six-time First-Team All-Pro and seven-time Pro Bowl selection spent 13 seasons with the Eagles and won a Super Bowl with the franchise. However, he does not believe his playing experience alone makes him the best candidate for the job.“I was there in training camp a little bit and learning the offense a little bit and trying to help those guys as far as, like, I think anybody who’s played a long time can offer a good perspective on how to help and assist in a room like that at a position that they played in,” said Kelce on SPORTSRADIO 94WIP. “I think that there’s probably people that are far more experienced and knowledgeable than I am.“…The reality is one, I don’t have the time to do that, and then two, in a meaningful way, like, I’ll try and help those guys out any way I can, and I still go in every once in a while but to offer the type of assistance you would be saying I don’t have that time, and then two, there’s just better people that have been offensive line coaches that, if they wanted to seek outside help, they could go to.”Jason Kelce's ESPN and podcast commitments keep him busyKelce's schedule helps explain his reluctance. He joined ESPN's Monday Night Countdown pregame show in 2024 and co-hosts the New Heights podcast with his brother, Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce. The podcast secured a reported $100 million deal with Amazon's Wondery, adding another major commitment to his workload.Family also plays a central role in his decision. Jason and his wife, Kylie Kelce, have four daughters, and the former center has repeatedly acknowledged the personal sacrifices required to coach in the NFL.“I would love to coach,” said Kelce. “The problem with coaching is the time — huge time commitment. If you want to be great at coaching, you can only coach and it takes away, especially if you want to do it at the NFL level. Potentially could do that in future at the high-school level. Definitely a different time commitment there. I want nothing to do with college.”For now, Kelce appears content with his life after football. He remains willing to offer advice to Philadelphia's players, but a full-time coaching return is not on his immediate agenda. The Eagles must look elsewhere for answers as they work to restore their offensive line's strength.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: From $15 an hour to a union: The long fight behind the Cowboys cheerleaders’ big win
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys have formally recognized their cheerleaders as a union.
articles.body: The Dallas Cowboys have formally recognized their cheerleaders as a union. The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders Association announced the move Friday, saying the team agreed after a "meaningful discussion." Bargaining can now begin, and no NFL cheer squad has ever reached a contract. The squad has 36 active members. Pay is the center of it. Until 2025, most veterans reportedly earned about $15 an hour. Getting from there to a bargaining table took years of organizing, and a Netflix series that carried the pay fight to a bigger audience.How $15 an hour became a bargaining tableStart with the money. In 2019, the Cowboys settled a lawsuit with a former cheerleader, and pay per game rose from $200 to $400. It helped. It was still small money.The bigger jump came in 2025. When season two of Netflix's America's Sweethearts: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders came out that June, one cheerleader revealed a 400 percent raise for the 2025-26 season. Veterans would make around $75 an hour, up from roughly $15 for most of the group. Those figures came from a cheerleader speaking on camera, so they are reported numbers, not a posted pay scale.None of it happened by accident. The cheerleaders worked together behind the scenes for years, and at one point they threatened to stage a walkout. Megan McElaney, one of the women who led the push for higher pay, said in the show's final episode, "Our efforts were heard." She added, "I get emotional knowing that I was a part of that."The team's own director backed the cause. Kelli Finglass called the effort to raise wages "60-plus years long overdue" on the show's second season. Coming from the person who runs the squad, that line carried weight.What the union can and cannot change yetRecognition is not a contract. Bargaining starts now, and nothing has been agreed on pay, hours or benefits. Early coverage does not list specific demands.The team did not force a fight over recognition. It agreed voluntarily, through a brief joint release with the cheerleaders' association. The statement praised the squad's talent and dedication. Pay terms were not in the portions quoted in early coverage. Voluntary recognition can spare a group a long fight over whether it may organize, so the cheerleaders can head straight to bargaining.If talks succeed, Dallas would be the first NFL cheer squad to reach a contract. Only one other team has tried to organize. The Buffalo Jills made a short-lived attempt in the mid-1990s, and it did not last.The cheerleaders also bring something most squads lack: a streaming audience. Two seasons of a Netflix show have made the pay fight easy for fans to follow, and hard for the team to ignore.The fight reaches well beyond Dallas. In 2014, Lacy Thibodeaux-Fields, then an Oakland Raiderette, sued her team. NFL cheerleaders have been pushing for better pay for a decade. Dallas is now believed to be the first pro cheer squad in the country with a union.Fans were quick to pick a side. The football team is 2-4, and one fan needled the team by saying the cheerleaders are the only ones winning. Another hoped the idea spreads to every NFL squad.The first real question is who gets a seat. The 2026 squad has 36 members, 28 returning veterans and eight rookies. It is still unclear how many the union will cover.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Brian Thomas Jr. Trade Linked to Super Bowl Hopefuls in New NFL Rumors, Why Jags 'Relented' Revealed
articles.summary: As Brian Thomas Jr.'s role in the Jacksonville Jaguars offense continues to diminsh, the team appears to be softening in their stance about moving him leading up to the trade deadline on Nov. 10.
articles.body:
As Brian Thomas Jr.'s role in the Jacksonville Jaguars offense continues to diminsh, the team appears to be softening in their stance about moving him leading up to the trade deadline on Nov. 10.

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler explained on SportsCenter that the Jaguars had "relented" on potentially trading Thomas in the past because of his talent, but now there is a feeling around the NFL that a deal could happen in the next few weeks with teams like the Kansas City Chiefs and Pittsburgh Steelers in the market for help at receiver:

"Brian Thomas Jr., immensely talented, but I've talked to several teams who believe he could be dealt over the next few weeks. Jacksonville has relented in the past. They've kept him because he's such a big talent. They hoped that his deep threat would balance things out with other receivers. The last two weeks, no catches, had just 15 snaps, so he was essentially benched in that London game against Houston. So, something has to give. There's going to be some interested parties. Kansas City's been looking around at potentially adding a receiver. Pittsburgh to some extent."

Thomas is coming off a game in Week 6 against the Houston Texans when he played a total of 15 offensive snaps.

Of the seven lowest snap-count games for Thomas in his NFL career, six have come this season. The only outlier was Week 8 of the 2024 season when he left in the third quarter against the Green Bay Packers due to chest and rib injuries.

Among Jaguars players, Thomas' 105 receiving yards are fewer than running back Bhayshul Tuten (126) and sixth-round rookie Josh Cameron (117).

Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers have clearly moved ahead of Thomas on the receiver depth chart.

Trading Thomas during the season might be the last time the Jaguars can get close to maximum value for him. He's still young enough, having just turned 24 on Oct. 8, for another team to believe in his ability to get back to the level he played at as a rookie.

Even if the Jaguars are ready to move on from Thomas, his potential landing spot will be worth monitoring.

The Jaguars are clearly established as a Super Bowl contender in the AFC, so trading Thomas to a team like the Chiefs or Steelers who they could end up meeting in the playoffs might make it hard for either of them to get a deal done.

One thing that does help Jacksonville's leverage is there are no shortage of playoff contenders in both conferences that could be in the market for a receiver.

Teams like the Los Angeles Rams, San Francisco 49ers, Washington Commanders are all dealing with at least one significant injury to a wide receiver.

Thomas' career arc to this point has been baffling. He looked like a superstar as a rookie in 2024 with 87 receptions, 1,282 receiving yards and 10 touchdowns in 17 games.

Since that time, though, Thomas has 57 receptions for 812 yards and three touchdowns in his last 20 games played. He is only owed $3.8 million in base salary through 2027.

articles.title: NFL House in Paris closes ahead of street protests in French capital
articles.summary: The NFL closed its “NFL House” in Paris on Saturday as the city braced for street protests with a heavy police presence and storefronts boarded up.
articles.body: PARIS — The NFL closed its “NFL House” in Paris on Saturday as the city braced for street protests with a heavy police presence and storefronts boarded up. The league announced the closure to fans on Saturday morning through its “OnePass” app and it came a day after it said its pop-up NFL shop would also be shut Saturday — in both cases citing “potential accessibility issues.” Security concerns have overshadowed the NFL’s debut in Paris. The New Orleans Saints will play the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday at Stade de France in the league’s first-ever regular-season game in France. Also Saturday, the Saints announced that “ Saints House has been postponed until Sunday.” Events planned Saturday at NFL House included “French Athletes in Football” and “From the Field to the Community.” “I was looking forward to just checking out some of the installations they had — they were going to have the Lombardi Trophy,” fan Nick Paiva said. Museums closed Major museums including the Louvre and Orsay Museum are closed Saturday, though tourists were lined up to enter Notre Dame Cathedral. French authorities are intent on preventing a repeat of recent violent unrest. The U.S. State Department this week issued a security alert that cautioned “Americans in Paris for the NFL game” to “exercise caution and be aware of their surroundings” because of protests. NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell said this week that preparations were made in consultation with U.S. and French authorities. Street protests, he said, “are not unusual in France.” On Friday, French President Emmanuel Macron met with Goodell along with Saints owner Gayle Benson and Steelers owners Art Rooney II at the Élysée Palace to “discuss Sunday’s game and the long-term future of the NFL in Paris.” The NFL said Friday that its pop-up shop in the city center would be closed Saturday but that fans could use an alternative shop set up at Stade de France, located north of the city in Saint-Denis. A weekend event for Steelers fans was canceled Thursday because of security concerns. Fans react in Paris Paiva, an American who lives in France, wanted to visit NFL House, where his partner, who is French, could learn more about the sport. He had also expected to participate in the league’s activation called “Hail Mary over the Seine” in which you try to throw a football across the famed waterway, at a location near Notre Dame. Despite having registered, Paiva was told at the site that he needed to also have made a time-slot reservation. “That was not communicated very well,” he said after being turned away. “C’est comme ca — it’s the way it is.” French teenager Oskar Le Gall, wearing a Bryce Young jersey, was able to give it a shot. His throw came up a bit short. A worker on the other side stayed busy scooping balls out of the river using a long pole with a net attached. Le Gall, who is from the Brittany region, said “the atmosphere of the NFL in Paris is amazing,” noting that French sports leagues and teams typically don’t promote themselves that much. Le Gall and his brother were keeping an eye on the planned path of the protests Saturday. “It doesn’t feel calm and good to be a tourist in Paris,” he said. “It’s not good for the NFL.” At one point during the Hail Mary event, 11 national police vans with their emergency lights flashing drove past on the street above as a fan got ready to throw a ball. Fan groups staying informed Steelers fan Monika Allen was able to avoid any protests thanks to advice posted on fan-led Facebook groups. “The fans are doing a good job keeping each other informed of where to be and where not to be,” Allen said by the ‘Hail Mary’ event. Her cousin, Viktor Toth, was wearing her Terry Bradshaw black-colored Steelers jersey. “We’re not worried,” she said. “My cousin is Hungarian, so he knows that the protests happen regularly in Paris.”

articles.title: 'Absolute S--t Show,' NFL Exec Defends Arch Manning, Top QBs as Scouts Question 2027 Draft Stock
articles.summary: Coming off back-to-back losses in which he did not play well, Texas quarterback Arch Manning still has supporters in the NFL after entering the season as a frontrunner to be the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 draft.
articles.body:
Coming off back-to-back losses in which he did not play well, Texas quarterback Arch Manning still has supporters in the NFL after entering the season as a frontrunner to be the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 draft.

Per The Ringer's Tom Pelissero , one NFL scouting director who defended Manning described trying to evaluate the 2027 quarterback class as an "absolute s--t show" in part because of how much roster and coaching turnover there is in college football:

"One NFL team's college scouting director cautioned against reading too much into the early-season play of Manning or any other quarterback, given how the transfer portal churns rosters and the impact a coordinator change can make if a player is struggling. But the scouting director also summed up the challenge of evaluating talent without any real sense of who will even be available next April: 'It's all an absolute s--t show.'"

Another interesting note from Pelissero is the amount of "skepticism" from people in the NFL about how many of the projected top quarterbacks eligible for the '27 draft will even declare, including Manning:

"Several high-ranking NFL executives and scouts expressed skepticism this week that some, if not a majority, of the projected top QBs will even enter the 2027 NFL draft. That includes Manning, who was the clear preseason favorite to be the no. 1 pick. He has struggled enough recently that his grip on the Longhorns' starting job could even be in jeopardy, with ESPN reporting Monday that redshirt freshman KJ Lacey Jr. would get an uptick in first-team reps this week in practice ahead of the Longhorns' game against Ole Miss. The once unthinkable possibility that Manning could transfer before he goes pro can't be ruled out. I talked about this with Bill Simmons on his show Thursday night."

A strong finish to the 2025 season had Manning's stock very high coming into this year. He was projected as the No. 3 overall pick by B/R's NFL scouting department in an early mock that dropped on Sept. 7.

Manning started this season with a marquee win over Ohio State on Sept. 12 in which Texas scored 21 points in the fourth quarter to erase a 23-3 deficit.

Even though Manning's numbers in that game weren't spectacular (195 passing yards, one touchdown and one interception), he was at the helm for all three of those touchdown drives that were at least 72 yards.

Since that victory against Ohio State, though, Manning has failed to capitalize on it. He has thrown for 795 yards, six touchdowns and three interceptions with a 62.3 completion percentage in his last four starts, including consecutive losses against Oklahoma and Florida.

The problem for NFL teams evaluating the 2027 quarterback class is many of the major prospects are injured right now.

Oregon's Dante Moore, who is B/R's No. 2 quarterback prospect, hasn't played since Sept. 26 due to a concussion. Ohio State's Julian Sayin (unranked by B/R) could miss at least the remainder of the regular season due to an injury suffered against Indiana on Oct. 17.

Players like Darian Mensah of Miami (B/R's No. 1 QB), Trinidad Chambliss of Mississippi (No. 3) and Drew Mestemaker of Oklahoma State (No. 7) have a strong opportunity to solidify their draft stock.

If those players feel like they are assured of being first-round picks in the '27 draft, it's hard to envision them turning down the guaranteed money that comes with it.

But if NFL teams express any skepticism that could push them into Day 2, the NIL money might be too much for them to resist going back to college for another season.

articles.title: Travis Kelce's $200 million Six Flags investment takes a hit as deadly accident forces major safety changes
articles.summary: Six Flags is preparing to strengthen safety measures on some of its biggest roller coasters after a fatal accident at its Georgia theme park raised fresh
articles.body: Six Flags is preparing to strengthen safety measures on some of its biggest roller coasters after a fatal accident at its Georgia theme park raised fresh concerns about ride safety. The decision comes as the amusement park operator works to improve guest confidence and business performance. Travis Kelce, the Kansas City Chiefs star who serves as a Six Flags ambassador and investor, adds another high-profile name to the company’s story. Although there is no indication that Kelce was involved in the safety decisions, the latest developments put the company’s operations and public image under renewed attention.Six Flags adds seat belts after fatal Goliath accidentSix Flags plans to install additional seat belts on the Goliath roller coaster at Six Flags Over Georgia and similar rides at other parks. The move follows the death of 42-year-old Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem, who fell from Goliath earlier this month. Investigators believe he was ejected from his seat, while four other passengers suffered injuries.The coaster already uses clamshell lap bars, which hold riders in place during the ride. However, the fatal incident has prompted the company to consider extra protection for passengers.Goliath stands about 200 feet tall and reaches speeds of up to 70 miles per hour. The ride has remained closed while authorities investigate what happened.Six Flags has also shut down eight other attractions across five parks as the investigation continues. The closures could affect visitors planning trips during the busy autumn season, while the company faces pressure to show that its rides meet strict safety standards.Chief Executive John Reilly said the company would bring in independent engineers and ride-inspection experts to review safety procedures across its attractions.“We are committed to carefully evaluating their findings and taking appropriate action to further strengthen our standards and culture of safety,” he said.The review could lead to broader changes in how Six Flags checks and maintains its rides.Travis Kelce’s Six Flags role draws attention amid safety reviewKelce’s connection to Six Flags gives the developments an added celebrity angle. The NFL star has a role as an ambassador and investor, linking his public profile to the amusement park business. However, there is no evidence connecting him personally to the Georgia accident or the company’s safety decisions.The incident also comes after Six Flags faced legal scrutiny over its X2 coaster at Six Flags Magic Mountain in California. Multiple lawsuits alleged that the attraction caused serious brain injuries. The company permanently closed X2 last month.Beyond safety, Six Flags has been working to improve ride reliability, maintenance and guest satisfaction. Those efforts matter because breakdowns, closures and safety concerns can affect attendance and the wider visitor experience.For Kelce and other investors, the company’s response will be important to watch as Six Flags works to rebuild confidence. The immediate priority, however, remains clear: establish what caused the fatal accident, complete the safety reviews and make sure guests can trust the rides they choose.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Top Landing Spots for Colts' RB Jonathan Taylor Amid Latest NFL Trade Rumors
articles.summary: The 2026 NFL trade deadline will arrive at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday, November 10. Between now and then, we can expect several notable players to be moved. Indianapolis Colts star running back Jonathan Taylor could be one of them.
articles.body:
The 2026 NFL trade deadline will arrive at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday, November 10. Between now and then, we can expect several notable players to be moved. Indianapolis Colts star running back Jonathan Taylor could be one of them.

While there's no guarantee that the Colts will engage in a fire sale following the firing of general manager Chris Ballard, it's possible. The Miami Dolphins took a similar approach last season after firing GM Chris Grier. Colts interim GM Ed Dodds will at least have to consider building for the future.

According to ESPN's Stephen Holder , "multiple teams" would be open to acquiring Taylor if he's a player that Dodds will make available.

With this in mind, let's examine the top landing spots for Taylor in 2026. We'll examine why these teams could (or should) pursue Taylor, how they could benefit the three-time Pro Bowler, and what each potential pairing could mean for the rest of the season and beyond.

First, though, let's dive a little further into Taylor's situation and his projected trade value.

Jonathan Taylor's Outlook and Trade Value

For many fans, the reaction to a report that multiple teams are interested in Taylor might be something along the lines of "well, obviously."

Taylor has long been one of the NFL's top running backs, best all-around players, and a legitimate dual-threat. He currently ranks seventh in the NFL with 655 scrimmage yards and is tied for sixth with seven combined rushing and receiving touchdowns. He's managed to thrive in a largely one-dimensional Colts offense that ranks 22nd in passing and 22nd in total yards.

In other words, Taylor is a legitimate difference-maker whose addition could transform a team's offensive identity—not wholly unlike the Kansas City Chiefs' offseason addition of Kenneth Walker III. Of course, there are other factors to consider in addition to Taylor's on-field ability.

For one, Taylor isn't clamoring for a change of scenery.

"I think it would be a discredit and a disservice to my teammates and this whole organization to think about what could, what should, what may be," Taylor said, per Holder .

Secondly, Taylor is under contract through 2029 and is set to see his base salary balloon to $15 million next season. While he's not necessarily old at 27, he's seen a good amount of wear and tear at the NFL level (1,875 touches in 90 regular-season games).

Additionally, any team acquiring Taylor would likely need to pay a hefty price tag.

Theoretically, he could be obtained as a short-term rental and released or dealt again before next year's pay bump—the prorated portion of this year's $7 million base salary would be reasonable, even for teams without a cap surplus. The Colts, though, won't value Taylor the same way.

Taylor has been the centerpiece of Indy's offense for several years, and moving him would cost the Colts $10 million in dead money next year.

The Colts will probably demand a first-round pick to begin negotiations, though a conditional second-rounder might be enough to get a deal done. Alternatively, a package of multiple Day 2 picks similar to the one the Carolina Panthers got for Christian McCaffrey in 2022 (2023 2nd-, 3rd-, and 4th-round picks, plus a 2024 5th-rounder) might suffice.

The McCaffrey trade is a reasonable comp, as he is a similarly skilled player and was 26 at the time of the trade.

The Denver Broncos have invested in their backfield over the past couple of seasons. They added J.K. Dobbins in free agency last year, used a 2025 second-round pick on RJ Harvey, and used a 2026 fourth-round pick on Jonah Coleman .

However, Denver's investments haven't yielded a quality rushing attack this season, a problem that has been compounded by the underwhelming play of quarterback Bo Nix.

The Broncos currently rank 30th in yards per carry, 31st in total offense, and 26th in scoring.

Injuries have been a piece of the equation—Harvey battled a hamstring strain early in the season, while Coleman was recently designated to return from an ankle sprain. Still, the Broncos' offense has been a mess this season, and Denver lacks the sort of do-it-all offensive weapon that Taylor has been throughout his NFL career.

Adding Taylor would help stabilize Denver's offense while Nix works through whatever issues have been behind his lackluster play. And the Broncos could treat his addition as a long-term investment since Dobbins looms as a likely 2027 cap casualty—cutting him in the spring would save $2 million in cap space.

Pairing Denver's defense with a backfield led by Taylor, Harvey, and Coleman could make the Broncos a formidable force for the next few seasons. Taylor, meanwhile, would get the chance to play for a perennial contender in a Sean Payton offense that would maximize his skill set.

The Seattle Seahawks—who, ironically, lost a sloppy game in Denver last week—share a few similarities with the Broncos. They've gotten less-than-ideal play from quarterback Sam Darnold (7 INTs), and they've struggled to field a high-end rushing attack.

Injuries have been part of the problem for Seattle, too, but the Seahawks currently rank 18th in yards per carry and 17th in total offense. That's simply not good enough for a team looking to repeat as Super Bowl champs.

Now, it's worth noting that Seattle wouldn't make as much sense for Taylor now as it might have a few weeks ago. The Seahawks recently designated Zach Charbonnet to return from last year's torn ACL, and first-round rookie Jadarian Price (chest) will be eligible to return from injured reserve early next month.

The Seahawks weren't willing to give Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker III a lucrative contract during the offseason, so why would they invest in Taylor when Charbonnet and Price are cheaper options?

The short answer is that Seattle needs to get Darnold back on track, and it lacks offensive playmakers behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Taylor's big-play ability and dual-threat skill set would help on both fronts.

The other factor to consider is that Charbonnet is set to be a free agent in 2027. If the Seahawks add Taylor, they could build a multi-year backfield tandem of Taylor and Price with the latter on a rookie deal during its duration.

Taylor would get to play for a Super Bowl-caliber team while potentially extending his career by working as part of a duo instead of as an every-down back.

The New York Giants aren't 2026 Super Bowl contenders in the mold of Seattle and Denver. However, New York is a promising up-and-coming team that is looking to build a competitive identity under new head coach John Harbaugh.

Despite losing second-year quarterback Jaxson Dart to a season-ending knee injury, the Giants remain in first place in the NFC East with a 3-2-1 record.

Unfortunately, New York is struggling to keep its offense on a successful path. The Giants will replace Jameis Winston with J.J. McCarthy as their starting quarterback for Week 7, and they're trying to figure out how to field a dependable running game.

Second-year back Cam Skattebo didn't touch the ball in Week 6, and Harbaugh recently lamented his team's lack of a reliable high-volume running back.

"I would love for us to be in that kind of a circumstance," Harbaugh said, per the team's official transcript . "A Derrick Henry circumstance or a Saquon Barkley circumstance or whatever it might be. That would be great, and we haven't.

Adding Taylor would give Harbaugh exactly the sort of every-down running back he wants. It would help the Giants navigate the rest of the season without Dart and would give them another centerpiece player around whom to build moving forward.

With all due respect to Skattebo, New York would probably feel much better about heading into 2027 with an offensive core of Dart, Taylor, and Malik Nabers.

While joining the Giants wouldn't give Taylor the chance to chase a championship in 2026, it might just put him in the playoffs. And it would allow him to be part of a promising rebuild in a big market for the first time in his career.

Taylor, it's worth noting, played his high school ball roughly two hours away form MetLife Stadium in New Jersey.

Taylor could prefer a return to the Midwest over a return to Jersey, given his experience as a star at Wisconsin. However, the Green Bay Packers might not be an ideal fit, now that Josh Jacobs has been removed from the commissioner's exempt list.

The Packers may not want to part with more high-end draft capital, as they still owe the Dallas Cowboys their 2027 first-rounder as part of the Micah Parsons trade.

Joining the Vikings in Minnesota might appeal to Taylor, though, and not just because of its locale. The Vikings are one of just three undefeated teams left in 2026, they have a championship-caliber defense, and they have a bevy of other playmakers in a potent Kevin O'Connell offense.

Taylor might get the chance to chase a Super Bowl in Minnesota, and he'd frequently face lighter boxes with Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison, and T.J. Hockenson threatening defenses deep.

The Vikings could use a back of Taylor's caliber, too. They're still trying to get new quarterback Kyler Murray into a rhythm, and if/when they do, a backfield featuring Murray and Taylor could be extremely dangerous.

Aaron Jones Sr. has been a fine starter for Minnesota thus far, but he missed time due to injury last season, will turn 32 in December, and will be a free agent in 2027. Jordan Mason is a capable complement and has been designated to return from his thumb injury, but he's also in a contract year.

Acquiring Taylor could give Minnesota an elite rushing attack in 2026 while also being a smart long-term play.

The Cincinnati Bengals may seem like an odd fit for Taylor at first blush. Cincinnati has a potent offense led by Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins. It has also had a very productive starter in Chase Brown in recent years.

However, Brown hasn't been very efficient this season (3.5 yards per carry), and the Bengals have looked for other ways to spark their 28th-ranked rushing attack.

"We got to be better," head coach Zac Taylor said following the Week 4 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars, per Pat Brennan of the Cincinnati Enquirer. "Especially after watching the tape, it's disappointing some of the plays we left out there. …We will be better moving forward."

Against the Miami Dolphins in Week 5, the Bengals found a spark by leaning on No. 2 back Samaje Perine. However, Perine has never been the sort of high-volume back that Taylor is, and he'll be a free agent in 2027, along with Brown.

Adding Taylor would give Burrow the sort of top-tier run support that he's rarely had in his NFL career. It would help Cincinnati potentially chase a championship this season while also stabilizing its backfield in 2027. And while adding him would be the sort of aggressive move the Bengals haven't historically made, they have taken a different approach this season.

The Bengals have made it clear that they're ready to maximize their window with Burrow now. They traded the 10th overall pick for defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence in the offseason, and they spent money on defensive free agents like Boye Mafe, Jonathan Allen, and Bryan Cook.

Turning back to the offensive side of the ball to add Taylor could be the move that finally makes Burrow and the Bengals perennial contenders.
